subject: Warmup latency and allocator lag — evidence packet and recovery plan
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@novaedge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-18T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: High warmup tail latency affecting NovaEdge (prod)

Hi Marissa,

We're seeing sustained tail latency spikes during our morning traffic ramp (US-PST) starting ~15:30 PDT. Approx 5-10% of requests to our dedicated pool returned 503 or 504 within 5-10s of the initial request; some requests also had token-generation timeouts. We've captured a set of sample request IDs: req_8241, req_8247, req_8259.

This appears correlated with autoscaler activity — when new nodes are brought up, the first minute of traffic shows very high latencies while warmup completes; for some requests allocations fail and we see request queue growth. Can Redwood temporarily route our traffic to a fallback model or increase dedicated concurrency? We need mitigation ASAP — this is impacting a small portion of production transactions.

Attached: small sample log lines and timestamps (see logs_bundle snippet).

Thanks,
Jessica Patel
Senior SRE, NovaEdge
ops@novaedge.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@novaedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-18T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High warmup tail latency affecting NovaEdge (prod)

Hi Jessica — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the sample IDs.

Immediate actions we've kicked off:
- Routed a small percentage of your traffic to the compatible fallback model (same family, lower memory) to reduce errors while we investigate.
- Opened an ops task to pin extra warm nodes for your pool during your morning ramp window.
- Requested a copy of the full logs and allocator traces (if you can share the bundle, it'll speed diagnosis).

Could you confirm the retention window and if any of the failing request IDs included function-calls/long output sequences (these delay warmup)? We'll keep you updated with targeted mitigation within the hour.

Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-19T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: High warmup tail latency affecting NovaEdge (prod)

Forwarding NovaEdge report — customer reports allocator-related failures during warmup. They sent a small logs bundle and sample request IDs. Please triage and propose a short remediation/maintenance plan we can offer.

Key asks from customer:
- Immediate reduction in 5-10% error surface (routing to fallback acceptable)
- Evidence of root cause and timeline for fix
- Request for credits if remediation requires traffic diversion or scheduled maintenance

Please include required rollback steps and expected customer impact.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-19T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High warmup tail latency affecting NovaEdge (prod)

I've pulled allocator and warmup traces from the customer logs they provided (attached: allocator_trace_0119.json) and cross-referenced with our control-plane metrics. Preliminary findings:

- Root cause: a race in the warmup scheduler where concurrent prewarm attempts hit allocator throttles; when multiple warmup workers request host allocations near-simultaneously, a throttling path rejects or delays allocation tokens leading to request queueing on the serving nodes.
- Trigger conditions: high ramp with bursty short-lived function-calls and variable sequence lengths; the autoscaler attempted to spin up ~6 nodes within 80s and the allocator returned transient ALLOC_THROTTLED responses in 2 windows.

Short-term remediation (safe):
1) Increase the warmup concurrency limit for NovaEdge pools to avoid simultaneous allocation spikes (config change).
2) Adjust prewarm threshold to keep 1-2 warm standby nodes for the first 15 minutes of expected ramp.
3) Deploy a small control-plane throttle-safety patch to retry allocation tokens with backoff (I attached hotfix_patch.diff).

I'll validate that the patch is non-disruptive and can be canary-released to a small percentage of NovaEdge traffic. Estimated time to canary release: ~90 minutes after approval.

Rollback: revert warmup concurrency and prewarm threshold to previous values; revoke patch via our normal config rollbacks (fast).

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-20T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High warmup tail latency affecting NovaEdge (prod)

Operational plan to propose to NovaEdge:

- Canary rollout of allocator throttle-safety patch to 5% of NovaEdge's pool traffic during off-peak (estimated window: 23:00-00:30 PST).
- Simultaneously increase warmup concurrency limit and set prewarm standby=2 for the ramping window.
- Monitor tail-latency (p95/p99), queue depth, and allocation error rates. If tail latency reduces and allocation errors drop to <1%, proceed to 25% then full rollout (typical 2-step ramp).
- Customer impact: brief 10-15 minute elevated errors possible during rollout; we will keep fallback model routing active until p99 drops below SLA thresholds.
- Credits: recommend offering a 20% one-month usage credit for dedicated capacity hours affected; legal sign-off required.

Attachments: evidence_packet_20260120.pdf, logs_bundle_20260119.tar.gz

Please approve the maintenance window and credit proposal so I can send formal communication to NovaEdge.

Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Manager
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@novaedge.com>, J. Patel <jessica.patel@novaedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-22T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Warmup latency — evidence, fix plan, and customer remediation commitments

Hi Jessica / NovaEdge team — thanks again for your patience. This is a consolidated update and the customer-facing evidence packet.

What we found:
- A race condition in the warmup scheduler produced transient allocation throttling during aggressive ramp events; that led to short windows where allocation calls were rejected and request queues grew.

What we did (immediate):
- Routed a portion of your traffic to a compatible fallback model to reduce errors while we prepared the fix.
- Applied a canary config change to increase warmup concurrency and set prewarm standby nodes during your ramp window.

Planned fix (next 48 hours):
- Rollout of a throttle-safety retry patch to allocator token requests (canary -> staged -> full).
- We'll maintain fallback routing until the staged rollout achieves p99 latency within SLA.

Compensation and evidence:
- We've attached the evidence packet and logs we used for diagnosis (evidence_packet_20260120.pdf, logs_bundle_20260119.tar.gz).
- We propose a 20% usage credit for one month applied to NovaEdge's Dedicated Capacity invoice for the affected window; Ben will follow up with the formal credit and PO path.

Next steps and timeline:
- Immediate: Ben to send maintenance window options and credit proposal (you should receive that within today).
- Full postmortem doc with root cause analysis, timeline, and mitigations will be delivered by 2026-01-29.

If you have any immediate constraints on a maintenance window (e.g., blackout periods), please flag them and we'll adapt.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: evidence_packet_20260120.pdf, allocator_trace_0119.json, hotfix_patch.diff

Marissa — appreciate the thorough update and the evidence packet. The proposed maintenance window (off-peak) works for us; we accept the 20% credit proposal pending formal PO.

Please proceed with the canary and keep us closely looped on p99 measurements. We'll stand by to adjust routing if any unexpected regressions appear.

Thanks,
Jessica
